sentences.text: Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans is a Gram-positive, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming, spindle-shaped bacterium first isolated from human faeces and described in 2013.
It forms a previously unknown line within the Blautia coccoides rRNA group, also called Clostridium subcluster XIVa.
Cultures ferment glucose and release lactic, formic, acetic and succinic acids as end products.
A study reported the species decreased in patients with active ulcerative colitis and increased in quiescent disease, and that it induced interleukin 10 from intestinal immune cells.
